1. Validate the current bill: confirm meter reads imply 863 kWh (35,198 − 34,335), line items sum to $183.20 ($18.79 + $49.64 + $114.77), and the change versus last month is +$37.58 ($183.20 − $145.62); treat any arithmetic mismatch as a suspected billing error.

2. Map both billing periods to tariffs: last month (2026-04-10 to 2026-05-11) and current (2026-05-11 to 2026-06-11) both fall under the post-2026-04-10 tariff (fixed $18.788; blended variable $0.0347738 + $0.13299 = $0.1677638/kWh for the first 2,000 kWh). Since rates are identical and days are equal (31 vs 31), set price_usd = 0 and days_usd = 0 unless a defensible daily proration applies.

3. Estimate weather_usd from NOAA degree days: compare last month (CDD 42 / HDD 221) to current (CDD 129 / HDD 67), derive a weather-to-kWh coefficient from bill history, convert the weather-driven kWh difference to dollars at the effective variable rate, or set weather_usd = 0 if no defensible coefficient can be estimated.

4. Compute usage_usd from the 107 kWh increase (756 → 863) valued at the effective rate, then set usage_usd as the residual so price_usd + days_usd + weather_usd + usage_usd equals exactly +$37.58.

5. Check for a billing error by comparing the tariff-modeled current-period total to the actual $183.20; if the difference exceeds rounding, set billing_error_suspected = true and billing_error_usd to the discrepancy, otherwise false and null.

6. Return only the JSON object with keys price_usd, days_usd, weather_usd, usage_usd, billing_error_suspected, and billing_error_usd.
